options: The energy an object has because it is moving
The energy stored in a stretched spring
The heat inside a warm room
The light used up by a screen
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is energy of motion — anything with mass that moves carries it.
questions.misconception: Stored energy (springs, heights) is potential energy, the frequent mix-up with kinetic.

questions.prompt: A 3 kg ball rolls at 2 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
questions.misconception: Skipping the ½ or the square gives 12 or 24 J; the half times the mass times speed squared is the recipe.

questions.prompt: A car doubles its speed. What happens to its kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Speed is squared in KE, so 2× the speed → 2² = 4× the energy.
questions.misconception: The 'double in = double out' intuition is the key trap; the square makes it four-fold.

questions.prompt: Two carts move at the same speed. Cart X is twice as massive. What ratio do their kinetic energies have?
questions.explanation: Mass appears once (not squared), so doubling mass doubles kinetic energy.
questions.misconception: Some carry the squaring habit over to mass — mass is only first power in the formula.

questions.prompt: In what unit is kinetic energy measured?
questions.explanation: Energy is measured in joules; newtons measure force, watts measure power.
questions.misconception: N (force) and W (power) get tangled with energy; the joule is the energy unit.
